title: How Burnham Can Make UK Devolution Work
gist: Truncated commentary opening: Andy Burnham has become UK prime minister and signalled his governing model on day one by pledging to end rough sleeping nationally via a scaled-up 'Housing First' strategy from Greater Manchester. Mazzucato's argument is that the first 100 days must go to institutional architecture, and that the real question is coordination between authorities rather than where power sits.

insights.claim: Andy Burnham, on his first morning as UK prime minister, visited a homelessness charity and pledged to end rough sleeping nationally by expanding the 'Housing First' strategy he ran as mayor of Greater Manchester.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: A new UK premiership whose first policy signal is centrally funded, locally delivered social housing points to where UK fiscal and housing-adjacent spend is headed.
insights.locator: LONDON—On his first morning as prime minister

insights.claim: Burnham's model of government is a state that provides resources from the center and then entrusts delivery — and the lessons that come with it — to local authorities.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: Central funding with local execution shifts UK procurement and contracting toward combined authorities and municipal bodies rather than Whitehall departments.
insights.quote: a state that provides resources from the center, then entrusts delivery—and the lessons that come with it—to local authorities
insights.locator: In doing so, he offered an early glimpse

insights.claim: The decisive constraint on devolved governance is not where decision-making authority is concentrated but whether different authorities are made to work together.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: Reframes UK devolution risk from a power-transfer story to an execution-capacity story — watch inter-authority coordination mechanisms, not headline devolution deals.
insights.quote: The question is not where to concentrate decision-making authority, but how to ensure that different authorities are working together.

insights.claim: Burnham's devolved-governance vision will fail unless his first 100 days as prime minister are devoted to building its institutional architecture.
insights.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato
insights.so_what: The first-100-days institutional build is the tell for whether UK devolution delivers real local delivery capacity or stalls — a timeline to monitor for UK domestic policy execution risk.
